competitive_landscape: Coastal transfers today are mostly road-based with catamaran excursions; the Mauritius–Réunion link is ferry/air. Large resort groups are natural partners; no foiling incumbent.

precedents.why_it_matters: Mauritius reproduces the large-resort-base transfer pattern with a regional Quanta-LR trunk layer.

regulatory_note: Mauritius flag; Mauritius Maritime Authority / Ministry of Blue Economy; resort groups control private jetties; Réunion link involves French/EU certification.
seasonality: Year-round; cyclone season Nov–Apr (calmer lagoons still operable); peak European demand Oct–Apr and Jul–Aug.
summary: Mauritius is a mature, high-volume luxury and mid-market resort destination ringed by lagoons, with heavy coastal transfer demand between Port Louis, Grand Baie, the west coast (Tamarin/Black River) and the southeast (Blue Bay/Mahébourg), plus excursion traffic to Île aux Cerfs and the northern islets. Longer Quanta-LR trunks open Rodrigues (~300 nm) and Réunion (~115 nm). The scale of the resort base and the lagoon-transfer pattern make it a strong island-hopping and ferry-upgrade market.
tagline: A large Indian Ocean resort economy with dense coastal-lagoon transfers and outer-island links to Rodrigues and Réunion.
